answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce deposit before it may submit claims, then slash that deposit when independent audits confirm fraud. Creating a thousand aliases no longer multiplies influence for free: each one ties up capital, and detected fakes lose it. Auditors can sample claims across a ripple of dependent transactions, while a karst-like network of shared funding links helps expose coordinated wallets. A fable about one honest agent is not proof; the bond makes deception costly at scale.
